newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market active at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market active at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Tuesday were fairly active, with sales at $70.00 per cwt, unchanged from Monday's top prices and down $1.00 from last week's tops, feedlot sources said.

About 11,000 head were reported sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, with 63,500 head confirmed for the week to date which included 16,200 formulated cattle and 200 contracts to be shipped this week, according to USDA.
In Kansas, about 15,800 head traded, with the week to date at 29,200 confirmed, including 1,400 head previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Monday's sales at $70.00 may have taken some packer buyers by surprise, sources said.
"I don't think they (buyers) really expected cattle owners to hit the lower bids so early in the week, but it hasn't stopped them from buying," one cattle feeder said.

The aggressiveness at which packers seem to be buying cattle at the lower prices so early in the week suggests they were short on supplies or were anticipating stronger beef business, the cattle feeder said.
Boxed beef prices near midday were quoted up $0.22 per cwt to down $0.21 on 216 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
